correctness.rationale: The coordinate-cross support E=(A×0)∪(0×B) has four disjoint overlap regimes. At mixed nonzero shifts the self-ambiguity is a sum of two unit character values; its ratio has odd order and cannot equal -1. At axial shifts exactly one character coordinate must be trivial, giving kernel n(m-1)^2+m(n-1)^2. Fourier-Weyl diagonalization gives singular values √(mn)|A_g| and row/column sum kernel constraints. For two prime-field axes, residues r u-s v are uniformly distributed over character pairs, yielding the full cosinusoidal spectral table and condition number (2p−1)/(2sin(π/(2p))). The graph of point pairs whose two coordinates both differ has diameter at most two for m,n≥3; diagonal and mixed-entry recovery therefore forces all nowhere-zero signals to differ only by unit global phase. Independently enumerated ambiguity for p=3,5, with exact zero counts; all-group theorem uses the overlap proof, not finite samples.
